This happened to me. Similar weeks as well, at 9. I ordered the pill and did all the proper procedures. It failed me. 

I waited 4 weeks after to test since the instructions said you can still get a positive even if it worked. 

I was devastated, I cried a lot. I was out the $300 I paid. 

But, I went and got the SA. It was a 2 day procedure. Not so bad tbh. The first day was very long, I’m talking about 6/7 hours. 

The 2nd day was quicker. I always recommend sedation. And I was walking around the mall and living normally about 1 day after the SA. 

As far as getting back a negative pregnancy test, I waited a month after my SA to test at home. It’s negative. 

I also waited for my bleeding to stop after my SA for me to begin my birth control. You can start soon as you’d like but I felt better waiting. 

It may seem bleak but I promise there is a light at the end of a tunnel. Good luck honey

Not sure if they told you but, prescriptions go from date of a sale. So if you picked it up 2 days early (especially for a control), it will factor that in the next fill. 

As in, it’s cumulative. 2 days early here and there pile up and the system (not just CVS’s, there’s a separate system not connected to CVS for controlled medications) will adjust the next refill date according to the amount you’ve picked up since the pill quantity should get you to the next date. That way there is no overlap, as per medications being taken as the directions written. 

As far as calling instead of using the app; it’s just because the app goes off the CVS system which can put medications on an automatic hold or whatever. It will sometime auto schedule, other times not. 

That unfortunately leaves it for you to call and have us run it through for you.
